narr: Tropical Cyclone Kay formed on September 4th, 2022 and made its closest approach to Southern California on the 9th and 10th, with the center of Kay coming within 120 miles of San Diego. Tropical moisture associated with Kay managed to produce heavy rainfall leading to flooding across mountainous terrain in Southern California on September 9th and 10th. This led to a number of wind damage and flooding events in the mountains and desert foothill locations in Southern California. Kay transitioned to a Post-Tropical Cyclone that weekend, but left enough lingering moisture to support additional rounds of heavy thunderstorms through the 11th and 12th of September. These later rounds of heavy rain would lead to multiple significant debris flow events in the San Bernardino County Mountains, namely in and around the Apple and El Dorado burn scars.
ev: Heavy rain associated with residual moisture from post-tropical cyclone Kay occurred during the afternoon on September 12 in southern portions of the Inland Empire. The Department of Highways reported a swift water rescue of a person seeking refuge on top of a vehicle. Heavy rain associated with residual moisture from post-tropical cyclone Kay occurred during the afternoon on September 12 in the San Bernardino County Mountains. Rain amounts of 1.5 to 3 inches occurred in the region. The Department of Highways reported a flash flood near Crestline, with multiple vehicles stuck in flood water on Lake Drive at Forest Shade Drive. Portions of Wildcat Canyon Rd on the Barona Reservation under 3-10 inches of running water due to heavy rainfall. Visibility reduced to 1/4 mile during rain.

Highway 18 between Waterman Canyon and Highway 138, heavy rain led to debris flows including boulders up to 1 foot in diameter across all lanes. Water several inches deep was also flowing across lanes.

Heavy rain from residual moisture associated with Tropical Cyclone Kay occurred across northern portions of the Inland Empire, leading to multiple instances of flash flooding. Flash flooding was reported by a trained spotter on University Parkway and Kendall Drive near Devore, with one foot of water covering the roadway. Farther south toward Rialto, flooding occurred across all lanes on I-215 northbound. Flooding was also reported near San Bernardino across all lanes from University Parkway to Mount Vernon Ave.
